description: The plot illustrates how GPU memory usage varies with the number of video frames for several models. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Frames,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 1000 with major ticks at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled “Memory (GB),” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 400 with major ticks every 50 GB. Five lines are shown: (1) a pink solid line with circular markers labeled “VideoLLaMB,” which increases gradually from roughly ~15–20 GB at the smallest frame count to about ~75 GB at 1024 frames; (2) an olive/gold solid line with circular markers labeled “VideoLLaMB-R,” rising from roughly ~15–20 GB at the smallest frame count to about ~38–40 GB at 1024 frames; (3) a green solid line with circular markers (legend text is obscured by a gray box), increasing from roughly ~15–20 GB at the smallest frame count to about ~75 GB at 1024 frames; (4) a teal solid line with circular markers labeled “LLaVA-NeXT,” increasing from roughly ~15–20 GB at the smallest frame count to about ~145 GB at 1024 frames, with intermediate points around ~45 GB near 256 frames and ~75 GB near 512 frames; and (5) a purple solid line with circular markers labeled “VideoLLAVA,” which rises steeply from about ~20–25 GB at the smallest frame count to around ~120 GB near 128 frames and ~230 GB near 256 frames, then continues upward beyond the plotted y-range (exceeding 400 GB) by around 320 frames.
